title: Unateness of linear threshold functions
statement: Let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and suppose there are real weights $a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_n$ such that $f(x)$ is the sign determined by whether $a_0+\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i$ is nonnegative. Then, in every coordinate, $f$ is either monotone or antimonotone: changing that coordinate from $-1$ to $1$ never decreases the function, or changing it from $1$ to $-1$ never decreases the function.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$f$ has a representation by real affine weights followed by the specified threshold-sign rule
